rubric.name: Landing page — ship or not
rubric.description: Decide whether an AI-generated landing page for a developer tool can go live.
rubric.context: A developer asked an AI coding agent for a landing page for their open-source developer tool and is deciding whether to publish it. The reader of the page is a developer who has never heard of the tool. The facts input says what is true about the tool; anything the page claims beyond it is invented.

criteria.name: First screen says what it is

anchors.fail: From the first screen alone a developer cannot say what the tool does, or only gets a slogan.
anchors.pass: From the first screen alone a developer can say in one sentence what the tool does and for what.

criteria.name: A next step on the first screen

anchors.fail: The first screen has no visible button, link or command telling the reader what to do next.
anchors.pass: The first screen shows a clear next step, such as an install command or a button to the code or docs.

criteria.name: The next step leads somewhere real

anchors.fail: The page claims something the facts do not support: testimonials or quotes, customer or company logos, user, download or star counts, speed or accuracy numbers, pricing plans, a sign-up or waitlist, or features the facts do not list.
anchors.pass: Every claim about users, customers, numbers, prices and features on the page is backed by the facts.

anchors.fail: On the phone-width screen, text or code is cut off, overflows sideways, overlaps, or is too small to read.
anchors.pass: On the phone-width screen, everything visible fits, does not overlap and can be read.
